newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UOB says Malaysia merger to boost growth.
newsitem.headline: UOB says Malaysia merger to boost growth.

text.p: Singapore's United Overseas Bank Ltd (UOB) said on Thursday the merger of its two Malaysian banking units was designed to boost its growth in the Malaysian market.

UOB chairman Wee Cho Yaw told reporters at a Singapore briefing the new bank, which he said would be the most profitable foreign-owned bank in Malaysia, would benefit from economies of scale and concentrate on profitable activities.
UOB announced earlier in Kuala Lumpur that its Chung Khiaw Bank (Malaysia) Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd would merge by the end of the first quarter of 1997.
After the merger, the bank would be the 11th largest in terms of assets, loans and deposits, UOB officials said.
Total assets of the merged bank as of June 30, 1996 would have been 10.3 billion Malaysian ringgit (US$4.12 billion). Shareholders' funds of the two units totalled 839 million ringgit, UOB said.
"If the bank wants to grow, you have to increase your capital base," Wee, who is also the bank's chief executive officer, told the briefing.
"We believe Malaysia will continue to be a good market and will continue to expand even after the turn of the 21st century," he said.
"The merger will allow us to expand our business in Malaysia," he added.

Wee said that after consolidation the new bank would expand more into fee-based activities and would aim to place new share issues in the Malaysian market through initial public offerings, and hoped to expand its stock broking activities.
UOB announced earlier on Thursday it was starting a joint venture stockbroking firm with Malaysia's Affin Holdings Bhd.
Financial services firm Affin had said previously it would have a 55 percent equity interest in the joint venture.
Wee said he was sure the new joint venture would be very successful. "I think we have a lot of synergy," he said.
Wee said that outside Singapore, Malaysia was UOB's fastest growing market, where the banking sector was consolidating rapidly.
He said he expected the current 37 banks in Malaysia to be reduced to possibly as few as 10 in the future, opening up opportunities, but increasing competition, for the remaining banks.

He said the newly merged Malaysian bank would have a total of 25 branches, some of which might overlap. "We will try to relocate some of our 25 branches. We hope Bank Negara will be reasonable and allow that."
Wee said UOB had originally considered listing one of its Malaysian units, but had now ruled that out in favour of the new merged bank.
He said UOB wanted to continue to own 100 percent of the Malaysian bank and knew that any listing would involve a reduction of its holding.
"It will continue to be 100 percent owned," he said. (US$1=2.52 ringgit)
